title: CI runs at milestones, not on every merge, and you get options on best practice
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 (waiting page, item 27): "Not only drop the exception, I merge so arbitrarily and can merge so often that frankly I still find the amount of CI used to be preposterous. I think there may be something in this roadmap already of essentially wanting \"milestone-style\" reviews of CI -- I think my Q_Max repo might have some examples of that where I got so sick of my CI bill that I was like look orchestrator after u see a ton has landed then yes run a check but not every merge. That could be me not doing best practices, and I'm eager to learn, and/but I want some help here"
note: Measured Oct 13-27 at main 2ad85de: about 16,800 runner-minutes a week; the run after each merge to main is 38% of it and ended green 4 of 48 times last week, mostly cut off at Windows and Chromium time caps. Item 27 (c69) answered a: drop the per-lane full CI job exception; the build advisor has it. Part 1 done Oct 27 (doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/XMDQP1nVCuq3u35qvwE8eV). Pick C, as proposed: one scoped run per batch, batches cut at about 4 waiting lanes or 3 hours, no run on main and no nightly, a full run at named milestones; about 2,400 minutes a week. Needs first: a trustworthy full run, and a batch proved against current main. Part 2 lands in the global CLAUDE.md (roles-each-layer-proves-once, git-integration-branch-merge) and the gates workflows. Answer, Oct 27 11:45 CDT (shiv, item 31): none of these; he leans to a mix and is not yet sure merges cause no regressions or that tests pin anything meaningful. Deferred (shiv, Oct 27): part 2's pick is his. Asked: waiting page item c95-ci-milestones, again 11:58 CDT with option (e), trust first then cut in steps (fix time-outs, mutation-check test value, count repaired merges; cut runs only past measured bars). Port: yes; the rule is global, each repo's workflows follow at its visit. Placed ahead of c82, after c88 (triage, Oct 27): CI spend grows with every merge. Ruling, Oct 27 12:07 CDT (shiv, item 31): pick (e), trust first then cut in steps, note 'a combo of a, c, e'. Reading built from: step 1 as (e) (full run stops timing out, a mutation check measures test value, merges that needed a repair are counted); step 2 takes q_max's shape (a: quick checks on each branch, full suite on main) in place of (b); step 3 ends at (c)'s milestone runs; each step only past its measured bar, and a missed bar steps back. Step 1 lanes queue with the build advisor.
